refreshed look, twelve more connectors, e-signature and secure documents, virus scanning, call tracking numbers, AI service targets, wellbeing signals, training offers, import from Genesys or Avaya, a browser extension, and two more messaging channels.

A refreshed look: a quieter menu (an icon rail with a panel for each section, and the tabs of a page as a sub-menu), pages and figures that are easier to read, campaign, queue and Settings pages split into tabs, wrap-up outcomes as tiles you can search, the flow designer as a workspace (step palette, a big canvas with zoom and Show all, and a panel for the chosen step or the flow's own settings), one colour for each agent state on every screen, and better use of wide screens and the dark theme.

Any web CRM: every finished call can be posted to your own CRM's API, with its key; click-to-dial and screen pop already work with it.

Connectors for Epic (FHIR), Guidewire and Pega are built and wait for a customer system to test with.

Connectors for Kustomer, Intercom, Gorgias and Freshservice are built and wait for a customer account to test with.

Google Conversational Insights: finished calls, chats and emails go, with personal details removed, to Conversational Insights in your own Google Cloud (Pending third party: a first live test).

Amazon EventBridge and Kinesis: send platform events straight into your own AWS event bus or data stream, alongside webhooks (Pending third party: a first live test).

E-signature: send a customer a document to sign from a ticket by SMS, WhatsApp or email; the signed copy with its audit trail lands on the ticket (Pending third party: DocuSign or Adobe Sign).

Secure documents: from a ticket, ask a customer to upload their documents by a secure link, or send them files they open with a one-time code.

Virus scanning: files customers send are scanned before agents open them; an infected file is blocked and admins are alerted (Pending: switching the scanner on).

Deepfake screening: calls can be checked for cloned or synthetic voices, the agent sees the result, and flows can route on it (off by default; Pending third party: a detection vendor).

Apple Messages for Business and RCS: two more messaging channels, ready to connect once Apple approves us and an RCS aggregator is signed (Pending third party).

Call tracking numbers: see calls, sales and cost per sale for each advertised number. Scripts can list words agents must say or must not say.

AI service targets: set targets for AI availability, errors, response time and outcomes per channel, and get an alert when one turns red. Operators, resellers and dealers see AI usage and spend across their tenants under Billing, and AI usage can be a scheduled report, including at the end of each billing cycle.

Wellbeing signals (off until you switch it on): team leaders see which of their agents show signs of strain, with the reasons and a suggested next step; agents can get a gentle nudge to take a breather.

Workforce: when a queue is quiet the offers rule can post a training window instead of leave early, and people plans show staff and hiring costs.

Import from Genesys or Avaya: bring people, agents with their skill levels, skills, queues, wrap-up and not-ready codes across from a Genesys Cloud or Avaya export, with a dry run first (Pending third party: tests with real export files).

Browser extension: agents call any phone number on a web page from their desk, from Chrome or Firefox (Pending third party: store listings; install the download meanwhile).

Your industry: set your organisation's industry in Settings, and the template pickers and the industry call-flow menu start on it.

Desk Recorder: it is now in the Chrome Web Store, and a desk that records without it shows a button to install it.

Queues board: the Tiles / List / Office / Queues switch on the floor shows its words again, so the board where you drag agents between queues is easy to find.

Script forms: more rules (does not contain, "}
